author_text: Arthur O. Lovejoy, Reflections on the History of Ideas

author_text: Arthur O. Lovejoy, Reply to Professor Spitzer
method_problem: defense of analysis and discrimination of Romanticisms against Geistesgeschichte

author_text: Abraham Edel, Levels of Meaning and the History of Ideas
method_problem: meaning is temporally/developmentally stratified rather than detachable once-for-all
analytic_operation: plot appearances and changing levels of meaning
context_causation_position: meaning develops in historical sequence; context enters into semantic development

author_text: Paul O. Kristeller, The Philosophical Significance of the History of Thought
method_problem: jurisdiction of history of thought across philosophy/literature/art/religion/science
analytic_operation: comparative historical analysis across disciplinary objects
context_causation_position: philosophical history shares field with other forms of intellectual history

author_text: Philip P. Wiener, The Logical Significance of the History of Thought
analytic_operation: clarify logical relations without reducing historical development to formal validity
article_use: Useful control for Lovejoy logic/jurisdiction branch

author_text: Roy Harvey Pearce, The Significances of the Captivity Narrative
method_problem: one apparent genre has changing cultural significances; content alone insufficient

context_causation_position: proper historical view requires form, impact, milieu as well as content; asks what narratives were for contemporary readers
relation_to_lovejoy: Lovejoy-trained Hopkins scholar before his 1948 method note

author_text: Roy Harvey Pearce, A Note on Method in the History of Ideas
method_problem: analytic pioneer phase vs synthetic second stage
analytic_operation: extricate ideas; trace origin/growth/mutation/collocation/interaction; then study contexts as idea-informed cultural processes
context_causation_position: history should ask how ideas enter, affect and function in specific cultural processes
primitive_nonwestern_relevance: primitivism + progress is his worked example of historically possible but logically discordant collocation

author_text: Maurice Mandelbaum, Arthur O. Lovejoy and the Theory of Historiography
method_problem: what theory of past/reconstruction underlies Lovejoy practice
context_causation_position: stresses Lovejoy's tracing of causal relations and pluralistic conception of past

author_text: Arthur O. Lovejoy, Historiography and Evaluation: A Disclaimer
analytic_operation: disaggregate specific logical/ethical claims before value judgment
article_use: Another jurisdiction firewall: historical identification before evaluation
